library.description: Runtime-neutral supervision for execution units and coroutines.

blocks.text: English
后台任务、子进程和工作线程迟早会出问题：启动就崩溃、跑着跑着卡死、停止时迟迟不退出。`@migaia/supervision` 替你看管它们：限制同时运行的数量，确认它真正准备好才交给你，失败后按递增的间隔重启，失败太多就停下并告诉你原因；停止时分段限时，旧实例真正退出后才释放它占用的名额。

items: 崩溃风暴：子进程因为配置错误一启动就退出，`on('exit')` 里的重启逻辑每秒执行上百次，CPU 和日志被打满。根因是重启没有间隔，也没有“失败多少次就放弃”的上限。
卡死却显示“运行中”：进程还活着，但已经不处理任何请求。只监听退出事件发现不了，需要定期检查它是否还在干活。
发布时新旧版本同时干活，或者中间断档：先停旧再起新，中间有一段没人处理请求；先起新再停旧，又可能两个版本同时消费同一条任务。
关闭卡住，或者留下孤儿进程：子进程不理会退出信号，发布脚本一直等；父进程被强制结束后，子进程继续占着内存。

输出：

blocks.code: hello world | 启动次数: 3

blocks.text: 很多项目用几行代码自己“守护”子进程：
用监督器时，重启间隔、重启上限、停止限时和“停止后不再重启”都由同一个对象负责，不需要在每个项目里重新写一遍。

items: 即使服务一启动就崩溃，也不会无限重启。 默认第一次等 250 毫秒，之后每次翻倍，最长 30 秒；60 秒内最多自动重启 5 次，之后再失败就进入 `terminal` 状态，并通过 `report` 交出一个 `SUPERVISION_EXHAUSTED` 错误。你的原始错误一直保留在它的 `cause` 链上。
即使任务不理会停止信号，`stop()` 也会按时返回。 停止分三段：等应用收尾、等正常退出、强制结束后等回收，每段默认 5 秒。但这个任务占用的名额要等它真正退出才归还，所以新任务不会和没停干净的旧任务挤在一起。
替换时可以先起新、再停旧。 `replace({ strategy: 'start-then-switch' })` 等新实例准备好后才切换，旧实例在切换之后才收到停止信号。
旧实例不会冒充新实例。 每次成功启动都有新的 `generation` 编号，迟到的旧结果不会覆盖当前状态。
协程、线程、子进程用同一套规则。 平台差异只放在“启动器”里，重启、健康检查和停止策略写一次就能用于三种执行方式。
保证不了的事情会直接告诉你。 启动器必须如实声明自己能做到什么（例如能否结束整个进程树）。默认要求所有保证都成立，否则创建时就报错；你可以显式选择 `best-effort` 接受降级，降级项会出现在 `inspect().degraded` 里。

blocks.text: 一个被监督的执行单元（unit，一次启动出来的协程、线程或子进程）会经历这些阶段：

1. 申请名额：向预算（budget）申请一个位置。满了就排队，或者直接被拒绝。 2. 启动：启动器（launcher）按规格（spec）创建这个单元。 3. 确认就绪：如果提供了 `ready`，等它通过；超过启动时限（默认 10 秒）算启动失败。 4. 运行：`start()` 返回 `ready`。如果配置了健康检查，监督器会定期检查它。 5. 出问题：崩溃、健康检查连续失败或超出资源限制，都会结束这个单元，然后按重启策略退避重启，或者进入 `terminal`。 6. 停止：`stop()`、`replace()` 或 `dispose()` 按三段限时结束它。 7. 归还名额：只有单元真正退出后，名额才回到预算里。

rows: 创建一组单元共享的名额。
监督在当前事件循环里运行、能响应取消的任务。
监督由启动器创建的子进程。
监督由启动器创建的工作线程。
启动、停止、替换和永久关闭。
观察状态变化，读取当前状态和最近一次退出原因。

blocks.text: 完整用法见 USEGUIDE.md。
根入口负责预算、启动尝试、运行中单元的生命周期、限时停止、重启策略、健康检查、能力准入和状态观察。`./coroutine` 增加协作式任务；`./process` 和 `./threads` 使用同一套根契约。
创建预算 `createUnitBudget({ kind, maxUnits })`，再把预算、匹配的 profile、启动器、规格和 `report` 回调交给 `createSupervisor`。调用 `start()`，只有结果是 `ready` 时才使用单元；用完调用 `dispose()`。

启动器必须在单元停止、并且自己持有的资源都关闭之后，才让 `handle.exited` 完成；`exited` 永远不会以错误结束。profile 负责校验规格、声明需要的能力、幂等地结束单元，并给已完成的退出状态分类。`report` 接收终态、清理失败、迟到的失败和能力降级诊断。健康检查在响应取消时如果以自己的错误失败，即使监控已经关闭，这个错误也会被报告；如果它只是以取消原因结束，就不会再报告一次。`inspect()` 和 `subscribe()` 只观察状态，不会启动单元。
预算返回 `{ kind: 'granted', lease }` 或 `{ kind: 'rejected', reason }`。每个获得的名额只释放一次，`release()` 可以重复调用。关闭预算会拒绝排队中和之后的申请，已经发出的名额继续有效，直到对应单元真正退出。嵌套预算的单元类型必须相同，释放时先还父预算、再还子预算。

默认值：启动时限 10 秒；启动超时与其他启动失败使用同一套重启和终态策略；`acquireUnit` 抛出的错误以 `LAUNCH_FAILED` 报告，原始错误在 `cause` 上。停止的三段（应用收尾、正常退出、强制回收）各 5 秒。重启默认 `on-failure`，初始间隔 250 毫秒，倍数 2，最长 30 秒，60 秒内最多 5 次。默认终态策略是停在 `terminal`，直到显式调用 `restart()`；配置 `cooldown` 后会安排一次不阻止进程退出的重试。健康检查默认每 5 秒一次，单次限时 2 秒，连续 3 次失败判定为不健康。预算默认排队，排队最多等 30 秒，每秒最多发出 8 个名额。需要确定的时间行为时，传入自己的 scheduler。

核心只依赖 `@migaia/lifecycle` 和 `@migaia/utils`。profile 可以用 `hooks.acquireUnit` 接收预先启动好的单元，用 `hooks.afterLaunch` 挂接附属资源，用 `hooks.onReady` 挂接监控或让单元失败，用 `hooks.inspectUnit` 提供只读快照。登记在 `unit.scope` 里的附属资源在 `exited` 之后释放；登记在 `unit.monitors` 里的监控在结束单元之前释放。
监督器产生的错误带有 `source: 'supervision'` 和一个 `SupervisionErrorCode`；被包装的原始错误保留在 `cause` 上，清理失败可以通过 `errors` 找到。交给 `report` 的被动观察失败和迟到的检查失败保持原对象。状态和预算结果是返回值，不会作为错误抛出。

启动器明确声明 `exit-observation: 'unsupported'` 时，强制终止后立即报告 `EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE` 并将该代记为 abandoned，不等待 `reapTimeoutMs`。诊断详情包含 kind、generation 和 capability。名额仍保留到真实退出，不能把无法观察当作已经退出；可观察退出但超时的路径仍报告 `REAP_TIMEOUT`，启动阶段的回收超时也保持原行为。
`./process` 提供不经过 shell 的进程规格、能力检查、资源用量监控、有上限的输出尾部、持久的进程记录与回收、父进程断开保护，以及可选的有上限预热池。它只定义启动器接口，自己不创建操作系统进程。
`./threads` 用同样的预算、重启、健康检查、替换和限时释放策略监督由启动器创建的线程。启动器把 `heap-limit` 和 `exit-observation` 声明为 `enforced` 或 `unsupported`；不能可靠观察退出的启动器必须配置健康检查。线程既不能隔离崩溃，也不能限制 CPU；需要这两项保证时选择进程。

选项校验：`health.intervalMs` 必须是大于零的有限数；`startupTimeoutMs` 可以为零，表示立即到期；`restart.mode`、`terminalPolicy.mode`、`isolation` 只接受列出的取值；`stop` 三段时限都可以为零。未知的替换策略会在排队或停止当前单元之前抛出带 `INVALID_OPTION` 的错误。预热池和监督器用同样的方式接收注入的 scheduler。
English
包的定位、亮点和心智模型见 README。本指南先按场景给出可以直接运行的示例，再说明协程、进程和线程三种执行方式的详细契约。

sections.id: 监督一个真实的子进程
sections.heading: 监督一个真实的子进程

blocks.text: 本包定义公开的 launcher 接口，不直接调用操作系统 API。生产环境由传输插件提供真实的 launcher。下面用户编写的最小 launcher 只说明接口，用定时器句柄演示退出，不创建真实子进程。
下面的示例句柄每次启动 200 毫秒后都以退出码 3 退出，模拟一个读错配置的索引服务。监督器每次崩溃后间隔一段时间重启，重启 2 次后仍然失败，就进入 `terminal` 并停止尝试。
输出：
第一行 `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` 是降级提示：示例启动器声明自己没有提供故障隔离，选择 `best-effort` 后监督器照常工作，但会把这一项报告一次，并记在 `inspect().degraded` 里。不写 `isolation: 'best-effort'` 时，创建监督器会直接抛出这个错误。
“重启成功”指新进程启动成功，不代表它之后不会再崩溃。这里没有提供 `ready`，所以进程一启动就算可用；真实服务应该提供 `ready`，例如等它在标准输出里打印“已就绪”，或者等一次连接成功。
默认规则：第一次重启前等 250 毫秒，之后每次翻倍，最长 30 秒；60 秒内最多自动重启 5 次，之后再失败，监督器进入 `terminal`。进入 `terminal` 时，`report` 会收到 `SUPERVISION_EXHAUSTED`，你的原始错误在它的 `cause` 链上。
输出：

blocks.code:
SUPERVISION_EXHAUSTED <- LAUNCH_FAILED <- EXIT_UNEXPECTED <- 配置文件缺失
start(): terminal | 启动次数: 4 | 占用名额: 0

blocks.text: 启动 4 次 = 第一次启动 + 3 次重启。`start()` 不会因为单元失败而抛错，它返回 `terminal`；失败细节交给 `report`，也可以从 `inspect().lastExit` 和 `inspect().terminalError` 读取。
进入 `terminal` 后，监督器不会自己恢复，除非你调用 `restart()`，或者配置 `terminalPolicy: { mode: 'cooldown', afterMs }` 让它冷却一段时间后再试一次。`restart: { mode: 'never' }` 表示任何失败都直接进入 `terminal`。

sections.id: 用心跳发现卡住的任务
sections.heading: 用心跳发现卡住的任务

blocks.text: 只监听“退出”发现不了卡住的任务。协程监督器可以要求任务定期调用 `heartbeat()`；超过 `heartbeat.timeoutMs` 没有心跳，就判定为不健康，结束这次运行并按重启规则重新开始。
下面的扫描任务每处理完一页报告一次心跳。第一次运行在第 3 页卡在一个不会返回的请求上。
输出：

blocks.code:
第 1 次运行：完成第 1 页
第 1 次运行：完成第 2 页
exit: unhealthy
第 2 次运行：完成第 1 页
第 2 次运行：完成第 2 页
第 2 次运行：完成第 3 页
exit: exited

blocks.text: 注意：协程和你的其他代码共用同一个事件循环，监督器只能“请求”它停下。卡在同步死循环里、或者完全不理会取消信号的任务，监督器无法强行结束，它占用的名额也不会归还（见限时停止与名额归还）。需要强制结束时，用子进程。
子进程和线程没有 `heartbeat` 选项，用通用的 `health: { check, intervalMs, timeoutMs, failureThreshold }`：默认每 5 秒检查一次，单次限时 2 秒，连续 3 次失败就判定为不健康。`heartbeat` 和 `health` 不能同时使用。
预算（budget）是一组监督器共享的名额。名额用完后，新的启动请求默认排队，最多等 30 秒；设置 `overflow: 'reject'` 时直接返回 `full`。预算还默认限制每秒最多启动 8 个，避免瞬间起一大批。
输出：

blocks.code:
开始导出 a.csv，同时运行: 1
开始导出 b.csv，同时运行: 2
开始导出 c.csv，同时运行: 2

blocks.text: `c.csv` 等到 `a.csv` 结束、名额空出来之后才开始。预算只能被同一类单元共用：协程、线程、进程各自使用自己的预算，`kind` 不一致时创建监督器会报 `INVALID_OPTION`。
`replace()` 用新的实例替换正在服务的实例，可以同时换一份新的规格（例如新版本的命令参数）。默认策略 `stop-then-start` 先停旧再起新；`start-then-switch` 先起新，新实例准备好后才切换，旧实例在切换之后才收到停止信号。后者需要预算里能同时容纳两个单元。
输出：

blocks.code:
v1 开始消费
v2 开始消费
切换: generation 1 -> 2
v1 停止消费
replace(): replaced
v2 停止消费

blocks.text: 新实例启动失败时，`replace()` 返回 `{ kind: 'failed', error }`，旧实例继续服务。新规格在停止旧实例之前就会被校验；未知的策略名会直接抛出 `INVALID_OPTION`。
`stop()` 分三段，每段默认 5 秒：

1. 应用收尾：如果提供了 `stop.beforeTerminate`，先让它完成手头的工作（`drainTimeoutMs`）。 2. 正常退出：请求单元退出，等待它真正退出（`exitTimeoutMs`）。 3. 强制回收：强制结束后等待实际退出（`reapTimeoutMs`），超时报告 `REAP_TIMEOUT`。如果启动器已明确声明 `exit-observation: 'unsupported'`，则立即报告 `EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE` 并按 abandoned 处理，不等待该回收窗口；诊断详情为 kind、generation 和 capability: `'exit-observation'`。重复释放不会重复报告。
`stop()` 一定会在这些时限内返回。但如果单元还没有真正退出，它占用的名额会一直保留，直到它真正退出为止。这样新任务就不会和一个没停干净的旧任务同时运行。
`EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE` 是能力边界，不表示线程卡死，也不表示退出已获确认。调用方应按 source/code 区分它与 `REAP_TIMEOUT`；需要真实退出保证时更换启动器。best-effort 准入时的 `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`、required 模式的准入拒绝以及 launch 阶段超时均不改变。
输出：

blocks.code:
report: REAP_TIMEOUT
stop() 已返回，占用名额: 1
这时再申请名额: full
任务真正结束
任务结束后，占用名额: 0

blocks.text: `stop({ graceMs })` 只缩短这一次的“应用收尾”时间。`kill()` 跳过前两段，直接强制结束。`stop()` 之后可以再次 `start()`；`dispose()` 之后监督器永久关闭，再调用 `start()` 会被拒绝。

sections.id: 父进程退出与遗留进程
sections.heading: 父进程退出与遗留进程

blocks.text: 父进程被强制结束时，子进程收不到正常的停止请求。有两件事要做：

items: 子进程这一侧：用 `createParentLossGuard` 在父连接断开时开始收尾，并保证在 `graceMs`（默认 5 秒）内退出。收尾完成时退出码为 0；超时或收尾失败时为 1。
父进程这一侧：用持久的进程记录（registry）登记每个启动的子进程。下次启动时，先调用 `reclaimOrphanProcesses` 清理上次遗留的进程。它只结束“指纹”仍然匹配的进程；如果原来的 pid 已经被别的程序复用，只删除记录，不会误杀。

blocks.text: 输出：

blocks.code:
进度已保存
退出码: 0
结束遗留进程 4101
已结束: [ 'a' ] | 已删除记录: [ 'a', 'b' ]

blocks.text: 给 `createProcessSupervisor` 传入 `registry: { port, namespace }` 后，监督器会在启动时登记记录、在进程真正退出后删除记录。使用 registry 时，启动器必须实现 `probe` 和 `terminateRecord`。某条记录回收失败时，它会保留下来供下次再试，失败以 `ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED` 报告。
`createPrewarmPool` 提前启动若干空闲进程。监督器 `start()` 时直接取用一个，省掉创建进程的时间；取用后监督器仍然会执行 `ready` 检查。预热池必须和监督器使用同一个预算、启动器和规格对象，预热进程同样占用预算名额。

sections.id: 协作式任务-协程-的完整契约
sections.heading: 协作式任务（协程）的完整契约

blocks.text: `expose(port)` 只能调用一次，第二次调用会在任务内部抛出带错误码的 `TypeError`。如果任务在 `expose` 之前就结束，`exposed` 会一直等待，`ready` 检查会等到启动时限。任务收到的 `signal` 在停止、替换和 `dispose()` 时触发；异步生成器还会收到一次 `return()` 请求。`exited` 总是以 `{ outcome: 'fulfilled' }` 或 `{ outcome: 'rejected', error }` 完成，不会以错误结束。自定义 AsyncIterable 的 `return()` 失败会立即报告，但 `exited` 要等进行中的 `next()` 结束才完成，名额也保留到那时。
协作式结束依赖任务自己结束。不理会取消的任务可能超过 5 秒的回收时限：监督器报告 `REAP_TIMEOUT`，把它记为 `abandoned`，并在它真正退出前一直保留预算名额。监督器不能打断同步循环，也不能把崩溃隔离在事件循环之外。因此 `fault-isolation` 能力是 `unsupported`；在默认的 `isolation: 'required'` 下请求这项能力会被拒绝。
`replace({ strategy: 'start-then-switch' })` 要求预算能同时容纳两个单元。新实例准备好、`switched` 事件发出之前，旧实例一直可用；之后旧任务才收到取消信号。`replace({ spec })` 在动当前单元之前先校验新规格。默认策略先停旧实例，再启动新实例。
任务调用 `heartbeat()`，或者从异步生成器中产出值时，可以使用 `heartbeat: { timeoutMs, intervalMs?, failureThreshold? }`。错过心跳会变成 `UNHEALTHY`，`cause` 链上有 `HEARTBEAT_MISSED`。`heartbeat` 和通用的 `health` 选项不能同时使用。

`@migaia/supervision/process` 是与平台无关的契约。你提供的启动器的 `launch(spec, context)` 必须不经过 shell 启动进程，只传递 `env.inherit` 里列出的环境变量和 `env.set`，从启动开始就通过 `context.output` 读取每个设为 `drain` 的输出流，并且只在进程和启动器自己持有的资源都关闭后，才让 `handle.exited` 完成。启动器必须生成一个在 pid 被复用时会变化的指纹，幂等地结束声明的进程树，并如实报告各项能力的强度。profile 本身从不调用平台的进程创建 API。

默认隔离要求是 `required`：缺少 `termination` 或 `fault-isolation` 保证时，创建监督器会抛出 `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`。调用方可以显式选择 `best-effort` 并查看 `degraded`，但这不会让启动器真正获得那些保证。要监控内存或 CPU 上限，启动器需要实现 `sampleUsage`；默认每 1 秒采样一次。`sampleUsage` 连续 3 次失败会把进程判定为不健康；一次成功的采样超过上限，进程会被立即结束。监督器和预热池都要求 `usage.intervalMs` 是大于零的有限数，`failureThreshold` 是正整数。每个输出流保留最近 65,536 字节。父进程断开保护默认给收尾 5 秒；预热的空闲进程默认保留 60 秒。

启动密钥（bootstrap）只能通过标准输入的前缀或专用的文件描述符传递，绝不能放在参数、环境变量、错误、快照或日志里。无法证明某种传递方式安全时，启动器必须把 `bootstrap-stdin` 或 `bootstrap-fd` 声明为 `unsupported`。Electron 的 `utilityProcess` 目前两种方式都不支持。Windows 上只有在启动器证明进程是在 Job Object 中创建的（或者先挂起创建、加入 Job Object 后再恢复，并处理好失败清理）之后，才能把进程树结束声明为 `enforced`。本包的内存测试不能证明这些平台保证。

持久回收：注入 registry，并在创建监督器或预热池之前调用 `reclaimOrphanProcesses`。回收只结束指纹仍然匹配的记录；pid 已被复用的记录只删除、不结束。失败的记录会保留，供下次再试。预热池使用和监督器相同的预算、启动器和规格对象；它启动空闲进程，但监督器取用后仍会执行就绪检查。`restart()` 和 `replace()` 会绕过过时的空闲进程。预热池和监督器使用相同的 id、registry 和 namespace 时，取用会沿用预热进程已有的持久记录及其退出清理；不同的拥有者各自登记记录。在补发缓冲输出或实时转发时，输出回调抛出的异常会被报告，但不会中断输出。registry 的 `list` 失败会以 `ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED` 收集并报告，`detail.step` 为 `list`，此时不会动任何记录。

`@migaia/supervision/threads` 提供与运行时无关的线程契约。你提供的启动器的 `launch(spec, context)` 创建一个线程，返回可以幂等结束的句柄。它的 `exited` 只能在线程代码停止执行后完成，而且不能以错误结束。如果一个 Web 风格的线程在 error 事件之后仍在运行，启动器必须结束它，并以 `{ code: null, error }` 完成 `exited`。仅仅发出结束请求，或者收到运行时的关闭标记，都不能作为线程已经退出的证据。如果 `context.signal` 已经被取消，启动器必须拒绝，而不是创建线程。

启动器必须如实声明 `termination: 'enforced' | 'monitored' | 'unsupported'` 和 `fault-isolation: 'unsupported'`。在 `required` 隔离要求下，`enforced` 或 `monitored` 的结束能力可以通过，`unsupported` 会被拒绝；`monitored` 不代表运行时会强制执行。启动器还要如实声明 `heap-limit: 'enforced' | 'unsupported'` 和 `exit-observation: 'enforced' | 'unsupported'`。只有 `heap-limit` 为 `enforced` 时才接受 `heapBytes`；`callWallTimeMs` 原样交给启动器，用于它面向调用方的操作。不能可靠观察退出的启动器必须配置 `health` 检查，这样无声退出或停滞的线程才能被发现并结束。监督器不采样堆内存，线程也没有单独的“正常退出”阶段：先执行可选的 `beforeTerminate`，然后调用一次 `terminate()`；退出可观察时在回收时限内等待，明确不支持退出观察时立即报告 `EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE`。这两种 abandoned 结果都不会释放尚未确认实际退出的预算名额。
需要隔离崩溃、限制 CPU、持久回收遗留单元或读取输出时，选择 `@migaia/supervision/process`。线程代码和宿主共用同一个进程，无法提供这些保证。各平台的适配器及其验证属于对应的适配包；本包的内存测试不代表 Bun、Deno、浏览器或 Electron 的线程结束行为已经被验证。

items: `health.intervalMs` 必须是大于零的有限数，周期检查不能以零间隔运行。
`startupTimeoutMs` 可以为零，表示启动立即到期。
`restart.mode` 只接受 `never`、`on-failure`、`always`；未知取值在创建时被拒绝。
`terminalPolicy.mode` 只接受 `stay` 或 `cooldown`。
`isolation` 只接受 `required` 或 `best-effort`。
`stop` 的三段时限都可以为零，表示立即到期。
未知的替换策略会在排队或停止当前单元之前抛出 `INVALID_OPTION`。预热池和监督器用同样的方式接收注入的 scheduler。

blocks.text: 中文

Background tasks, child processes and worker threads fail sooner or later: they crash on startup, hang while still "running", or refuse to exit when you stop them. `@migaia/supervision` looks after them for you. It caps how many run at once, hands a unit to you only after it is actually ready, restarts it with a growing delay after a failure, and gives up with a clear error when failures pile up. Stopping is bounded in time, and a unit's slot is released only after the unit has really exited.

items: Crash loops. A child process exits right after start because of a bad config, and the restart in your `on('exit')` handler fires hundreds of times a second, flooding CPU and logs. The restart has no delay and no "give up after N failures" limit.
Hung but "running". The process is alive but no longer handles anything. Listening for exit cannot catch this; something has to check periodically that it still makes progress.
Overlap or a gap during deploys. Stop-then-start leaves a window where nobody serves requests; start-then-stop can let two versions consume the same job.
Shutdowns that hang, or orphans left behind. A child ignores the exit signal and your deploy script waits forever; after the parent is killed, children keep holding memory.

blocks.text: Many projects "babysit" a child process with a few lines like these:
With a supervisor, restart delay, restart limit, stop deadlines and "do not restart after stop" belong to one object, instead of being rewritten in every project.

items: A unit that crashes on start is never restarted forever. The first retry waits 250 ms and each later one doubles, up to 30 s. At most 5 automatic restarts happen within 60 s; the next failure moves the supervisor to `terminal` and sends a `SUPERVISION_EXHAUSTED` error to `report`. Your original error stays on its `cause` chain.

`stop()` returns on time even if the task ignores the stop signal. Stopping has three phases: let the application drain, wait for a normal exit, then force and wait to reap. Each defaults to 5 s. The unit's slot, however, is released only when it really exits, so new work never piles onto a unit that has not finished stopping.

Replacement can start the new unit before stopping the old one. `replace({ strategy: 'start-then-switch' })` switches only after the new unit is ready; the old unit receives its stop signal after the switch.
An old unit cannot pass itself off as the new one. Every successful start gets a new `generation` number, so late results from an old unit never overwrite current state.
One set of rules for coroutines, threads and processes. Platform differences live only in the launcher; restart, health and stop policies are written once and apply to all three.

Guarantees it cannot keep are reported up front. A launcher must declare honestly what it can do, for example whether it can end a whole process tree. By default every guarantee is required and construction fails otherwise; you may opt into `best-effort`, and the missing guarantees appear in `inspect().degraded`.

blocks.text: A supervised unit (one started coroutine, thread or child process) goes through these stages:

1. Get a slot. It asks a budget for a place. When the budget is full it queues or is rejected. 2. Launch. The launcher creates the unit from its spec. 3. Confirm readiness. If you supply `ready`, the supervisor waits for it. Missing the startup deadline (10 s by default) counts as a failed start. 4. Run. `start()` returns `ready`. With health checks configured, the supervisor checks the unit periodically. 5. Fail. A crash, repeated failed health checks or a resource limit ends the unit; the restart policy then backs off and retries, or moves to `terminal`. 6. Stop. `stop()`, `replace()` and `dispose()` end the unit within the three stop phases. 7. Release the slot. The slot returns to the budget only after the unit has really exited.

blocks.text: See USEGUIDE.en.md for complete usage.

Runtime-neutral supervision for execution units. The root entry owns unit budgets, attempts, active-unit lifecycle, bounded teardown, restart policy, health checks, capability admission, and observation. The `./coroutine` entry adds cooperative tasks; other unit profiles use the same root contracts.

Create a budget with `createUnitBudget({ kind, maxUnits })`, then pass that budget, a matching profile, a launcher, a specification, and a `report` callback to `createSupervisor`. Call `start()` and use the unit only when its result is `ready`. Call `dispose()` when finished. The complete coroutine example is in USEGUIDE.en.md.

The launcher must fulfill `handle.exited` only after its unit has stopped and its own resources are closed. `exited` never rejects. The profile validates specifications, declares required capabilities, terminates idempotently, and classifies fulfilled exit statuses. `report` receives terminal, cleanup, late rejection, and degraded-capability diagnostics. A health check that rejects its own failure while responding to cancellation is still reported after monitor closure; the exact cancellation reason need not be reported again. `inspect()` and `subscribe()` expose state without creating a unit.

Budgets return `{ kind: 'granted', lease }` or `{ kind: 'rejected', reason }`. Release each granted lease once; `release()` is idempotent. Closing a budget rejects pending and future admissions while existing leases remain held until their units actually exit. Nested budgets share the unit kind and release parent before child.

The default startup timeout is 10 seconds. A startup timeout follows the same restart/terminal policy as other startup failures and publishes a stable readiness result; acquireUnit failures are LAUNCH_FAILED with the original cause, even before a lease exists. Stop uses 5 seconds each for drain, graceful exit, and force reap. Restart defaults to `on-failure`, with 250 ms initial delay, factor 2, 30 seconds maximum delay, five restarts in 60 seconds. The default terminal policy stays terminal until explicit restart; a configured cooldown schedules one unref'd retry. Health checks default to a 5 second interval, 2 second check timeout, and three consecutive failures. Budget defaults are queue overflow, 30 second queue timeout, and eight grants per second. Supply a scheduler for deterministic timing.

The core depends only on `@migaia/lifecycle` and `@migaia/utils`. A profile may use `hooks.acquireUnit` for a preacquired unit, `hooks.afterLaunch` to own attachments, `hooks.onReady` to own monitors or fail the unit, and `hooks.inspectUnit` for a read-only snapshot. Attachments registered in `unit.scope` release after `exited`; monitors registered in `unit.monitors` release before termination. Unit-specific entry points belong beside, never inside, the root implementation.

Supervisor-created failures carry `source: 'supervision'` and one semantic `SupervisionErrorCode`; wrapped original failures remain on `cause`, and cleanup failures remain reachable through `errors`. Passive observer and late-check failures sent to `report` retain their original objects. States and budget outcomes are values, not thrown codes.

When a launcher explicitly declares `exit-observation: 'unsupported'`, forced termination immediately reports `EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE` and marks the generation abandoned without waiting for `reapTimeoutMs`. Details include kind, generation and capability. Its lease remains held until actual exit: an unavailable observation is not an exit receipt. Observable exit that misses its deadline still reports `REAP_TIMEOUT`; launch-phase recovery timeouts also retain their existing behavior.

The `./process` entry adds a shell-free specification, capability checks, usage monitoring, bounded output tails, durable orphan records and recovery, a parent-loss guard, and an optional bounded prewarm pool. It defines a launcher port and does not start an operating-system process itself. See USEGUIDE.en.md for the process contract, defaults and cleanup.

The `./threads` entry supervises a launcher-owned thread with the same core budget, restart, health, replacement, and bounded release policy. The launcher declares `heap-limit` and `exit-observation` as `enforced` or `unsupported`; a launcher without enforced exit observation requires a health check. A thread is not a fault-isolation or CPU-limit boundary. Choose the process profile when either guarantee is required. See USEGUIDE.en.md for the thread launcher contract and example.
`health.intervalMs` must be finite and greater than zero, so recurring health checks cannot run at a zero interval.
`startupTimeoutMs` may be zero for an immediate one-shot startup deadline.
`restart` selects a supported mode and bounded exponential backoff; unknown modes fail option admission.
`terminalPolicy` selects stay or cooldown; unknown modes fail option admission.
`isolation` accepts required or best-effort; unknown modes fail option admission.
`stop` defines drain, exit and reap phases. Their one-shot budgets may be zero for an immediate deadline.

An unknown replacement strategy throws coded `INVALID_OPTION` before enqueuing or retiring the serving unit. The prewarm pool snapshots its injected scheduler through the same lifecycle admission as the supervisor.

blocks.text: This module defines a public launcher interface and never calls operating-system APIs itself. Production transports provide real launchers. The user-written launcher below only illustrates that interface, using a timer-backed handle rather than creating a child process.

The example handle below always exits with code 3, 200 ms after starting, like an indexing service that reads a broken config. The supervisor waits between restarts; after 2 restarts it still fails, so the supervisor moves to `terminal` and stops trying.
Output:

The first line, `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, is a degradation notice. The example launcher declares that it provides no fault isolation. With `best-effort` the supervisor works normally, reports the gap once and records it in `inspect().degraded`. Without `isolation: 'best-effort'`, creating the supervisor throws this error instead.

"Restart succeeded" means the new process started; it says nothing about whether it crashes later. This example passes no `ready`, so a process counts as usable as soon as it starts. A real service should pass `ready`, for example waiting for a "ready" line on stdout or for one successful connection.

Default rule: the first restart waits 250 ms and each later one doubles, up to 30 s. At most 5 automatic restarts happen within 60 s; the next failure moves the supervisor to `terminal`. At that point `report` receives `SUPERVISION_EXHAUSTED`, with your original error on its `cause` chain.
Output:

blocks.code:
SUPERVISION_EXHAUSTED <- LAUNCH_FAILED <- EXIT_UNEXPECTED <- config file missing
start(): terminal | launches: 4 | slots in use: 0

blocks.text: Four launches are the first start plus 3 restarts. `start()` never throws because a unit failed; it returns `terminal`. Failure details go to `report` and are readable from `inspect().lastExit` and `inspect().terminalError`.

Once `terminal`, the supervisor does not recover by itself unless you call `restart()`, or configure `terminalPolicy: { mode: 'cooldown', afterMs }` so it tries once more after a cool-down. `restart: { mode: 'never' }` sends every failure straight to `terminal`.

sections.heading: Detect a stuck task with heartbeats

blocks.text: Listening for exit cannot catch a task that is stuck. A coroutine supervisor can require the task to call `heartbeat()` regularly. If no heartbeat arrives within `heartbeat.timeoutMs`, the run is declared unhealthy, ended and restarted under the restart rules.
The scanner below sends a heartbeat after each page. On its first run it gets stuck on page 3, waiting for a request that never returns.
Output:

blocks.code:
run 1: page 1 done
run 1: page 2 done
exit: unhealthy
run 2: page 1 done
run 2: page 2 done
run 2: page 3 done
exit: exited

blocks.text: A coroutine shares the event loop with the rest of your code, so the supervisor can only ask it to stop. A task stuck in a synchronous loop, or one that ignores the stop signal entirely, cannot be forced to end, and its slot is not released (see Bounded stop and slot release). Use a child process when you need a forced stop.

Processes and threads have no `heartbeat` option. They use the generic `health: { check, intervalMs, timeoutMs, failureThreshold }`: by default a check every 5 s, 2 s per check, and 3 consecutive failures mean unhealthy. `heartbeat` and `health` cannot be combined.

sections.heading: Limit how many run at once

blocks.text: A budget is a set of slots shared by several supervisors. When every slot is taken, a new start queues by default for up to 30 s; with `overflow: 'reject'` it returns `full` immediately. A budget also allows at most 8 starts per second by default, so a burst cannot start everything at once.
Output:

blocks.code:
exporting a.csv, running: 1
exporting b.csv, running: 2
exporting c.csv, running: 2

blocks.text: `c.csv` starts only after `a.csv` finishes and frees its slot. A budget serves one kind of unit: coroutines, threads and processes each need their own budget, and a mismatched `kind` fails supervisor creation with `INVALID_OPTION`.

`replace()` swaps the serving unit for a new one, optionally with a new spec such as new command arguments. The default `stop-then-start` stops the old unit first. `start-then-switch` starts the new unit first and switches only when it is ready; the old unit receives its stop signal after the switch. The latter needs a budget with room for two units.
Output:

blocks.code:
v1 consuming
v2 consuming
switched: generation 1 -> 2
v1 stopped
replace(): replaced
v2 stopped

blocks.text: If the new unit fails to start, `replace()` returns `{ kind: 'failed', error }` and the old unit keeps serving. A new spec is validated before the old unit is touched; an unknown strategy name throws `INVALID_OPTION` right away.
`stop()` has three phases, 5 s each by default:

1. Application drain. If you passed `stop.beforeTerminate`, it finishes in-flight work first (`drainTimeoutMs`). 2. Normal exit. The unit is asked to exit and the supervisor waits for the actual exit (`exitTimeoutMs`). 3. Forced reap. After a forced stop, the supervisor waits for actual exit (`reapTimeoutMs`) and reports `REAP_TIMEOUT` on expiry. If the launcher explicitly declares `exit-observation: 'unsupported'`, it immediately reports `EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE` and abandons that generation without waiting for this window. Details contain kind, generation and capability: `'exit-observation'`. Repeated disposal does not repeat the report.
`stop()` always returns within these deadlines. If the unit has not really exited, though, its slot stays occupied until it does, so new work never runs next to a unit that has not finished stopping.

`EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE` identifies a capability boundary, not a stuck thread or confirmed exit. Branch on source/code to distinguish it from `REAP_TIMEOUT`; choose another launcher when actual-exit guarantees are required. Best-effort admission's `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, required-mode admission rejection and launch-phase timeouts remain unchanged.
Output:

blocks.code:
report: REAP_TIMEOUT
stop() returned, slots in use: 1
asking for a slot now: full
task actually ended
after the task ended, slots in use: 0

blocks.text: `stop({ graceMs })` shortens only this call's drain phase. `kill()` skips the first two phases and forces the stop. You can `start()` again after `stop()`; after `dispose()` the supervisor is closed for good and `start()` is rejected.
When a parent process is killed, its children never receive a normal stop request. Two things help:

items: In the child, `createParentLossGuard` starts cleanup when the parent connection drops and guarantees an exit within `graceMs` (5 s by default). The exit code is 0 when cleanup completes and 1 on timeout or cleanup failure.

In the parent, a durable registry records every child it starts. On the next start, call `reclaimOrphanProcesses` first to clean up what the previous run left behind. It ends only processes whose fingerprint still matches; if the old pid now belongs to another program, it removes the record without killing anything.

exit code: 0
ending leftover process 4101
terminated: [ 'a' ] | records removed: [ 'a', 'b' ]

blocks.text: Pass `registry: { port, namespace }` to `createProcessSupervisor` and the supervisor adds a record when it starts a process and removes it after the actual exit. With a registry, the launcher must implement `probe` and `terminateRecord`. A record that fails to reclaim is kept for the next attempt, and the failure is reported as `ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED`.

`createPrewarmPool` starts idle processes ahead of time. When a supervisor calls `start()`, it takes one instead of spawning, and still runs its `ready` check afterwards. The pool must use the same budget, launcher and spec objects as the supervisor, and every idle process occupies a budget slot.
Output:

blocks.code:
idle processes: 1
start(): ready | idle left: 1

blocks.text: Taking an idle handle triggers replenishment. This example launcher returns immediately, so one idle handle has already been refilled when `start()` completes.
An idle process that nobody takes within 60 s (the default) is ended. `restart()` and `replace()` skip idle processes that may be stale and start fresh ones.

`expose(port)` may be called once. A second call throws a coded `TypeError` inside the task. If the task ends before exposure, `exposed` remains pending, so the readiness hook waits until the startup deadline. The task's own signal aborts on stop, replacement, and dispose. Async generators also receive one `return()` request. `exited` always fulfills with `{ outcome: 'fulfilled' }` or `{ outcome: 'rejected', error }`. For a custom AsyncIterable, a rejected return request is reported immediately, but exited remains pending until the outstanding next finishes. Its lease is retained until that actual exit.

Cooperative termination depends on the task settling. A task that ignores cancellation can outlive the 5 second reap deadline. The supervisor reports `REAP_TIMEOUT`, records `abandoned`, and retains its budget lease until the task actually exits. It cannot preempt a synchronous loop or isolate a crash from the event loop. The `fault-isolation` capability is therefore `unsupported`; requests for it are rejected under the default `isolation: 'required'` policy.

`replace({ strategy: 'start-then-switch' })` needs a budget with room for two concurrent units. The old port stays usable until the candidate is ready and the `switched` event fires; then the old task receives cancellation. `replace({ spec })` validates the new specification before touching the active unit. The default strategy stops the old unit before launching the new one.

Use `heartbeat: { timeoutMs, intervalMs?, failureThreshold? }` when the task calls `heartbeat()` or yields from an async generator. A missed heartbeat becomes `UNHEALTHY` with `HEARTBEAT_MISSED` on its cause chain. `heartbeat` and the generic `health` option are mutually exclusive.

`@migaia/supervision/process` is a platform-neutral contract. Supply an adapter whose `launch(spec, context)` starts without a shell, transfers only the named `env.inherit` keys plus `env.set`, drains every `drain` stream from startup through `context.output`, and fulfills `handle.exited` only after the unit and adapter-owned resources have closed. The adapter must generate a fingerprint that changes across pid reuse, terminate the declared process tree idempotently, and report capability strengths honestly. The profile itself never calls a platform spawn API.

The default isolation is `required`; a missing `termination` or `fault-isolation` guarantee rejects construction with `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`. A caller may explicitly select `best-effort` and inspect `degraded`, but this does not improve the adapter's actual guarantees. A monitored memory or CPU limit requires `sampleUsage`; sampling defaults to 1 second. Three consecutive sampleUsage rejections mark the unit unhealthy; a successful sample exceeding a monitored limit terminates it immediately. The supervisor and prewarm pool both require a finite positive usage.intervalMs and a positive safe-integer failureThreshold. Each output tail keeps the latest 65,536 bytes per stream. The parent-loss guard defaults to a 5 second shutdown grace period; prewarm idle units default to 60 seconds.

Bootstrap bytes travel only as a stdin prefix or dedicated fd. Never put them in arguments, environment, errors, snapshots or logs. The adapter must declare `bootstrap-stdin` or `bootstrap-fd` as `unsupported` when it cannot prove that carrier safe. Electron `utilityProcess` currently has neither approved bootstrap carrier. Windows tree termination may be declared `enforced` only after an adapter has proved creation inside a Job Object, or suspended creation followed by assignment and resume, including failure cleanup. The profile's in-memory tests do not establish those platform guarantees.

For durable recovery, inject a registry and call `reclaimOrphanProcesses` before creating a supervisor or pool. Recovery terminates only a record whose fingerprint still matches; reused pids are removed without termination. Each failed record stays available for another attempt. An optional prewarm pool uses the same budget, launcher and specification objects as its supervisor. It starts idle units but the supervisor still performs readiness after taking one. `restart()` and `replace()` bypass stale idle units. When pool and supervisor use the same id, registry port and namespace, adoption reuses the exact warm durable record and its actual-exit cleanup. Distinct owners register their own records. Output sink exceptions during buffered replay or live forwarding are reported without stopping delivery. A registry list failure is collected and reported as ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED with detail.step set to list; no record is touched.

`@migaia/supervision/threads` owns a runtime-neutral thread contract. Supply a launcher whose `launch(spec, context)` creates a thread and returns an idempotently terminable handle. Its `exited` promise must fulfill only after thread code stops executing, and must never reject. An error event that leaves a Web-style thread running requires the adapter to terminate it and fulfill `exited` with `{ code: null, error }`. A termination request or a runtime close marker alone is not evidence of actual exit. If `context.signal` is already aborted, the launcher must reject without creating a thread.

The launcher must declare `termination: 'enforced' | 'monitored' | 'unsupported'` and `fault-isolation: 'unsupported'` truthfully. Required isolation accepts enforced or monitored termination, and rejects unsupported termination; a monitored declaration does not promise native enforcement. It also declares `heap-limit: 'enforced' | 'unsupported'`, and `exit-observation: 'enforced' | 'unsupported'` truthfully. `heapBytes` is accepted only when `heap-limit` is enforced; `callWallTimeMs` is passed unchanged to the launcher for its caller-facing operations. A launcher without enforced exit observation requires a `health` check so a silent exit or stalled thread can be stopped. The supervisor performs no heap sampling and has no separate graceful thread phase: it drains the optional `beforeTerminate` hook and requests `terminate()` once. Observable exit waits up to the core reap deadline; explicitly unsupported exit observation reports `EXIT_UNOBSERVABLE` immediately instead. Either abandoned outcome keeps its budget lease occupied until actual exit.

Use `@migaia/supervision/process` when you need crash isolation, a CPU limit, durable orphan recovery, or output draining. Thread code shares the host process and cannot provide those guarantees. Platform adapters and their runtime-specific proof belong to their owning module; this profile does not assert that Bun, Deno, browser, or Electron thread termination has been verified by its in-memory tests.
`health.intervalMs` must be finite and greater than zero, so recurring health checks cannot run at a zero interval.
`startupTimeoutMs` may be zero for an immediate one-shot startup deadline.
`restart` selects a supported mode and bounded exponential backoff; unknown modes fail option admission.
`terminalPolicy` selects stay or cooldown; unknown modes fail option admission.
`isolation` accepts required or best-effort; unknown modes fail option admission.
`stop` defines drain, exit and reap phases. Their one-shot budgets may be zero for an immediate deadline.

An unknown replacement strategy throws coded `INVALID_OPTION` before enqueuing or retiring the serving unit. The prewarm pool snapshots its injected scheduler through the same lifecycle admission as the supervisor.
